In [[modal logic]], '''van Benthem's theorem''' characterizes propositional modal logic as the [[Fragment (logic)|fragment]] of [[first-order logic]] that is invariant under [[bisimulation]]. The theorem was proven by [[Johan van Benthem (logician)|Johan van Benthem]] in his doctoral thesis, ''Modal Correspondence Theory'' (1976).<ref>{{Cite book |last=van Benthem |first=Johan |title=Modal Correspondence Theory |publisher=Instituut voor Grondslagenonderzoek, University of Amsterdam |year=1976}}</ref> A formal statement and game-theoretic proof of van Benthem's theorem is provided by Otto.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Otto|first=Martin|title=Elementary Proof of the van Benthem-Rosen Characterisation Theorem|date=2004}}</ref>

== Formal Statement ==
The following is based on Otto.<ref name=":1" /> Consider [[Formula (logic)|formulas]] in [[first-order logic]] with the [[Signature (logic)|signature]] <math>(E, P_1, \dots, P_n)</math>, where <math>E</math> is a binary relation symbol and <math>P_i</math> are unary relation symbols. A [[Kripke model]] <math>\mathcal A = (A, E^\mathcal A, P_1^\mathcal A, \dots, P_n^\mathcal A)</math> is a [[Structure (mathematical logic)|structure]] with the same signature. A pointed Kripke model is a pair <math>(\mathcal A, a)</math> where <math>\mathcal M</math> is a [[Kripke model]] and <math>a \in A</math>. We write <math>(\mathcal A, a) \sim (\mathcal B, b)</math> if <math>(a, b) \in R</math> for some [[bisimulation]] <math>R</math>. 

A formula with one [[Free variables and bound variables|free variable]] <math>\varphi(x)</math> in first-order logic is ''invariant under bisimulation'' if for all pointed Kripke models <math>(\mathcal A, a), (\mathcal B, b)</math>, <math>(\mathcal A, a) \sim (\mathcal B, b)</math> implies that <math>\mathcal A, a \models \varphi(x) \Leftrightarrow \mathcal B, a \models \varphi(x)</math>. 

Van Benthem's theorem states that the following are equivalent:

* <math>\varphi(x)</math> is invariant under bisimulation.
* <math>\varphi(x)</math> is [[Logical equivalence|logically equivalent]] to a formula in propositional [[modal logic]].
The statement above shows that the fragment of first-order logic invariant under bisimulation can be translated into propositional modal logic. The converse is given by the [[standard translation]], which shows that every formula in modal logic can be translated into a formula in first-order logic. These formulas are invariant under bisimulation, since modal logic is invariant under bisimulation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hennessy |first=Matthew |last2=Milner |first2=Robin |date=1985-01-01 |title=Algebraic laws for nondeterminism and concurrency |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2455.2460 |journal=Journal of the ACM (JACM) |location=New York, NY, USA |publisher=Association for Computing Machinery |volume=32 |issue=1 |pages=137–161 |doi=10.1145/2455.2460 |issn=0004-5411}}</ref>

== Similar Results ==
While van Benthem showed that the theorem holds over the class of (finite and infinite) Kripke models, Rosen showed that the theorem also holds over the class of finite Kripke models.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rosen |first=Eric |date=1997-10-01 |title=Modal Logic over Finite Structures |url=https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1008275906015 |journal=Journal of Logic, Language and Information |volume=6 |issue=4 |pages=427–439 |doi=10.1023/A:1008275906015 |issn=1572-9583}}</ref>

Theorems analogous to van Benthem's theorem have been found for various modal logics. For example, Janin and Walukiewicz showed that [[modal μ-calculus]] is the fragment of [[monadic second-order logic]] invariant under bisimulation.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Janin |first=David |last2=Walukiewicz |first2=Igor |date=1996 |editor-last=Montanari |editor-first=Ugo |editor2-last=Sassone |editor2-first=Vladimiro |title=On the expressive completeness of the propositional mu-calculus with respect to monadic second order logic |url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/3-540-61604-7_60 |journal=CONCUR '96: Concurrency Theory |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |pages=263–277 |doi=10.1007/3-540-61604-7_60 |isbn=978-3-540-70625-0}}</ref>
